summary: The revised policy accurately limits reliance on the fixed A–E PIT batches, but its copy-paste focused-run examples do not meet the newly required evidence-retention procedure.

findings.title: Focused PIT example discards the required console log
findings.trigger: A changed root-package class is absent from the A–E patterns, so a maintainer substitutes that class into the focused `targetClasses` command shown here.
findings.consequence: The Maven/PIT output is only printed to the terminal, leaving no command log to copy with the XML; the resulting evidence cannot satisfy the required durable focused-run record or support later failure review.
findings.evidence: The focused command at `verification/pit.md:65-69` has no redirection or log capture, and the generic focused command at `verification/pit.md:91-95` has the same omission. The new rule at `verification/pit.md:116-119` requires capturing the full invocation output before archiving it. In contrast, `scripts/run-pit-core.sh:195-199` clears stale output and redirects both streams to `pit.log`.
findings.suggestedFix: Update both focused-run examples to create a durable evidence directory, redirect Maven stdout and stderr into its `pit.log`, and copy `core/target/pit-reports/mutations.xml` there. If documenting `tee`, require pipefail so a Maven failure remains visible.
